text:
support: HS-4102 — customer reports spike in p95/p99 latency for the continuous-batcher path (chat generation). Started ~yesterday evening after a config push. p95 went from ~120ms to 420ms, p99 to ~1s. customer repro included curl against /v1/generate with prompt set A. They see high tail on small requests.

sam: looking. which cluster/region?

support: us-west-2 (hosted). affected model: gpt-medium-ql8 (quantized variant). Customer says requests are typically 16-64 tokens.

julia: I have the alert graph — p99 spike aligns with a rollout at 2026-03-10 22:10 UTC that tweaked batcher defaults (min_wait_ms increased from 2 to 10, max_batch_size bumped to 128).

miguel: ah, we changed tiny_wait for continuous batcher to reduce tiny batches; that will increase wait for small requests. Could explain p95 bump.

anna: customer is sensitive to p99 < 500ms. Current p99 ~980ms for that route. They want a mitigation asap.

sam: quick mitigation options — rollback config, limit that route to smaller max_batch_size, or reduce min_wait_ms. Rollback easiest but noisy.

kevin: can we do a targeted route override (route-level policy) rather than global rollback? If we lower min_wait for this customer route to 3ms we should drop tail.

julia: we have route overrides in the control plane. I can push a canary with policy: {"min_wait_ms": 3, "max_batch_size": 64} to that customer only.

miguel: also consider enabling prefix KV cache for that model and workload; many small requests repeat prefixes. Cache reduces per-token compute and avoids re-batching in some cases.

support: customer asked for repro steps — including a sample request and logs. They say curl got 850ms on their side.

sam: paste their repro and I’ll run from our infra to confirm.

support: (pasted) ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-medium-ql8","input":"summarize: short text","max_tokens":32}'
```

sam: ran it 10x against production route — median ~130ms, p95 ~410ms, p99 ~920ms. Local reproduce ✅.

miguel: can we capture batcher logs for those requests? Need to see if requests are waiting the full min_wait window or piling up into big batches.

anna: ops-bot, dump last 5k batcher events for route prod/gpt-medium-ql8 in us-west-2.

ops-bot: @anna scheduled job: retrieving batcher-events (5k) for prod/gpt-medium-ql8/us-west-2... done. Output: /var/tmp/batcher_events_1960001234.log

sam: quick scan — majority of requests at the p99 were served in batches of 64–128 with average batch latency = 480ms. But there are many small 1–4 request batches waiting near the min_wait boundary. So increase in min_wait caused the small requests to sit longer while waiting to hit higher batch size.

julia: that matches the timeline. Yesterday's change favored throughput (pack bigger batches) at the expense of tail latency for small, low-token workloads. We didn't anticipate some customers with latency SLOs.

miguel: proposed immediate mitigations:
- route override to {min_wait_ms: 3, max_batch_size: 64} for the affected customer (canary)
- enable prefix cache if applicable
- add temporary throughput headroom by routing this customer's requests to dedicated pool with prewarmed instances (if customer has Dedicated)

sam: I'll push the route override now. Julia, can you create the control-plane patch? Make it canary=on and TTL 2h.

julia: creating patch. CLI snippet:```json
{
  "route": "acct/6789/routeA",
  "overrides": {"batcher.min_wait_ms": 3, "batcher.max_batch_size": 64},
  "canary": true,
  "ttl": "2h"
}```

julia: applied canary override.    :rocket:

sam: re-ran the customer's curl 10x — new p99 ~220ms, p95 ~160ms. Major improvement.

support: customer confirms lower tail. They asked why the global change was made and whether we can avoid regressions.

miguel: root cause is config change that increased min_wait to favor efficiency. We need better guardrails:
- require perf evaluation matrix for config changes that affect batching (simulate p95/p99 on representative prompt sets)
- automated canary to incrementally roll batcher config per route instead of global jump
- a guard in deploy pipeline that flags routes with latency SLOs (from tenant metadata) and prevents increase of min_wait above X

kevin: add to postmortem but also short-term: add an alert that watches p99 delta > 2x following config changes in control plane within 24h.

anna: opened ticket SRE-912 with summary and links to logs/graphs. assigning @miguel for root cause and @julia for control plane rollback/canary improvements.

miguel: will run a synthetic workload harness across typical small-request customers to tune default min_wait. I propose default min_wait = 5ms, tiny_wait path = 1ms for tiny requests under 8 tokens.

sam: also add docs for customers: "Why your small requests sometimes see more tail latency" and include recommended settings for latency-sensitive customers.

support: customer satisfied with canary result, keeping ticket open to monitor for 48h.

ops-bot: alert suppressed for prod/gpt-medium-ql8/us-west-2; suppression TTL 2h (owner: sam).

kevin: quick note — cost tradeoff: lowering min_wait increases compute and may increase token cost per request. Customer agreed to trade cost for latency for now. Add billing note to ticket.

miguel: follow-ups:
- SRE-912: RCA + recommendations (due 48h)
- CP-1847: control plane guardrails for batcher changes (PR queue)
- DOCS-452: customer-facing guidance

sam: closing the immediate escalation. Monitoring until 1960001402. If p99 creeps back we'll revert. :eyes:

support: thanks all. customer follow-up sent.

julia: filing a short post-deploy checklist item to run the batcher-sim locally for each config change that touches min_wait or max_batch_size.

sam: note for runbook: when investigating tail spikes in continuous batcher: 1) check recent batcher config pushes, 2) inspect batch size distribution and min_wait, 3) try route override canary, 4) consider prefix caching and dedicated routing.

support: marking this thread resolved for now.
